title: Workflows, agents and who runs the steps

items.stem: A vet clinic's intake script sends each owner message to a language model with the instruction "reply with exactly one label: BOOKING, BILLING or EMERGENCY". The script then uses an if/else on the label to run the booking form, the billing lookup or the on-call pager code. Who decides what happens after the label comes back?

options.text: The model, because its label is what selects the next action
Both share it, because each message leads to a different outcome
The script, because the branches were written before any message came
The model, because a language model is called somewhere in the flow

items.stem: A lab's nightly job reads each new safety-incident form, extracts its fields, assigns a severity category, writes a two-line summary and emails it to the safety officer. All four stages run, in that order, for every form, and the group has a small model budget. Which statement about cost is accurate?

options.text: A fixed chain spends one call per stage; a model-run loop adds calls that only choose steps
Both cost about the same, since the same four stages must happen in either design
A model-run loop is cheaper, since the model can skip stages a given form does not need
A fixed chain is cheaper only because code is free, not because it makes fewer calls

items.stem: A grad student needs a tool to find out why a nightly simulation job failed. One failure is explained by the first log, another needs a config file checked next, and another needs the logs of a crashed node fetched after that. Each next check depends on what the last one showed, and new kinds of failure appear every month. Which design fits best?

options.text: A fixed chain that runs every diagnostic in order, then has the model summarize all results
A loop where the model picks each next diagnostic from the last result until it can explain
A fixed chain with an if/else branch per known failure type, extended as new types appear
A fixed chain where the model names the failure type, then code runs one preset diagnostic list

items.stem: A clinic booking system must verify a patient's insurance before it confirms any appointment, with no exceptions. A teammate proposes giving a model-driven assistant a verify_insurance tool and a prompt that says "always verify insurance before booking". In one or two sentences, why does that not give the guarantee the clinic needs, and what design would?

A 3D-printer lab's support bot has code that has a model label each question JAMMED, BED-LEVEL or FILAMENT, then runs a preset sequence for that label. The three sequences work well and cover about two-thirds of questions. The rest are varied, rarely repeat, and now get a generic apology. What is the best next step?

options.text: Replace the whole bot with a loop where the model chooses every step, even for the three working cases
Keep adding labeled branches until the unmatched share falls to near zero, then stop
Swap in a stronger model for the labeling step so that fewer questions fall outside the labels
Keep the three branches in code and send every unmatched question to a model-run loop with tools

items.stem: Before launch, a QA lead wants to feed a fixed sample input to each stage of a bot, check that stage's output on its own, and later rerun just one stage after editing its prompt. Which design makes this straightforward, and why?

options.text: A model-run loop, because each tool call is a step whose result can be checked on its own
A model-run loop, because its final answers can be compared with stored expected answers
A fixed chain, because every run passes through the same stages with known inputs and outputs
A fixed chain, because code stages never vary, so they need no checking at all
